title: Austin's ballot, and the paperwork behind it
subtitle: Two disclosure deadlines missed, 35,000 registrations late, Monday is the cutoff
alt: Timeline of the paperwork behind Austin's November 3, 2026 ballot, as reported by Community Impact and KXAN. Austin City Council candidates had to file a Statement of Financial Information by August 24, 2026, and eight candidates missed that deadline. They had to file a Personal Financial Statement by September 8, and seven missed that one; the city's Ethics Review Commission said missed filings are a recurring pattern election after election. Overnight on September 22 and 23, about 32,000 voter registration records that the Texas Department of Public Safety had failed to forward arrived at the Travis County Tax Office in one batch, pushing the county's total of delayed DPS records past 35,000; some had been submitted nearly a year earlier. The deadline to register to vote in the November 3 election is Monday, October 5. Early voting begins October 19, and Election Day is November 3, when Austin voters decide five City Council races, a bond election and Proposition I.
